title: 01 - LLMs, agents, and harnesses
description: Start from zero: define the model, agent, harness, SDK, and first query.
prompts: What is a large language model (LLM)? Explain in plain words what it can and cannot do.
What is an AI agent? Compare it with one ordinary LLM question-and-answer call.
What is an agent harness? Explain how it supplies instructions, tools, permissions, and a runtime.
Show how an LLM, an agent, a harness, and an environment fit together in one simple example.
What is the Claude Agent SDK, and which parts of an agent does it help me run?
What do I need to install and configure before trying my first local SDK query?
What is `query()` in the Python Claude Agent SDK? Explain its input and the messages it yields.
Show the smallest Python `query()` example and explain each line.
Explain how an agent uses tools, in simple words.
Compare a model, an agent, a tool, and a tool result using one student app.

title: 02 - Queries and results
description: Read the SDK event stream and its final outcome.
prompts: Walk through a query from user prompt to final result, one event at a time.
Show a short Python `async for` loop that handles AssistantMessage and ResultMessage.
What is the difference between an assistant message and a final result?
Explain why a tool request may lead to another model turn.
How should I recognize an incomplete or failed agent run?
Explain a result subtype in simple words and show how to inspect it.
What should I record from the final result for a student review?
Show how to collect readable answer text without losing the run status.
Why should I check the terminal result before saying the task succeeded?
Give me a tiny test that distinguishes a successful run from an error result.

title: 03 - Instructions and context
description: Shape requests without confusing source material with instructions.
prompts: Compare a user prompt and a system instruction with a small SDK example.
Rewrite a vague agent request into a specific goal and success check.
Show how to ask for a short answer with one verified code example.
How do I separate an uploaded document from my instructions to the agent?
Explain prompt injection using one harmless document example.
Show a prompt that asks Claude to say when the source is insufficient.
How can I ask for citations without inventing a source I did not provide?
Compare a short task prompt with a reusable system instruction.
How should I limit the context sent to a small student project?
Give me a checklist for reviewing whether the answer followed the request.

title: 04 - CLAUDE.md and project memory
description: Keep project instructions in the right place and verify what the SDK loads.
prompts: What is a CLAUDE.md file, and how is it different from one user prompt?
Write a tiny CLAUDE.md for a Python student app with its uv, ruff and pytest commands.
Which facts belong in CLAUDE.md, and which belong in a task-specific prompt?
Show how the `cwd` and `setting_sources` options affect loading a project CLAUDE.md.
Compare project CLAUDE.md, user CLAUDE.md, and a custom system prompt.
How can I verify that an SDK run received the intended project instructions?
What happens if `setting_sources` is an empty list when I expect CLAUDE.md to load?
Rewrite a long CLAUDE.md as concise, checkable project guidance.
Explain why secrets and temporary chat history should stay out of CLAUDE.md.
Give me a test that compares an agent run with and without project instructions.

title: 05 - Tools and permissions
description: Understand what tools can do and how to bound them.
prompts: Explain a tool call and tool result with a tiny Python example.
When should an agent use a tool instead of answering from context?
Compare read-only and write-capable tools for a local project.
What should an allowed-tools list contain for a read-only teaching agent?
Explain how to deny an unsafe tool call without claiming the run crashed.
Show a simple approval step before a tool changes a file.
How can I verify that a reported file change has a matching tool event?
Explain the difference between limiting a tool and removing it entirely.
Give me two tests for a tool: one valid input and one invalid input.
Draft a concise permission policy for an agent that reviews source code.

title: 06 - Skills and reusable workflows
description: Package reusable instructions in SKILL.md and check discovery and invocation.
prompts: What is an Agent Skill, and how does it differ from a prompt or a tool?
Show the smallest useful SKILL.md with a name, description, and three steps.
Where should a project Skill live so a local SDK session can discover it?
Show a Python `query()` that enables project Skills using `cwd`, `setting_sources` and the Skill tool.
Explain progressive disclosure: metadata first, SKILL.md when relevant, resources as needed.
How should I write a Skill description so the agent chooses it for the right task?
Compare automatic Skill selection with explicitly invoking a named Skill.
How can I verify that a Skill was actually loaded and used in a run?
What should I review before allowing a downloaded Skill to run scripts or read files?
Give me a small test for a Skill that formats a student report consistently.

title: 07 - MCP and external sources
description: Connect external knowledge deliberately and inspect evidence.
prompts: Explain MCP servers, tools, and resources with a simple diagram in words.
When would official documentation MCP improve an SDK answer?
Show a minimal server-side plan for connecting one read-only MCP source.
What should I check before trusting information returned by an MCP tool?
Explain why connecting an MCP server does not prove it was called.
How do I record which MCP tool supplied each claim in an answer?
Compare an answer using supplied documents with one using an external MCP source.
What should the app show when the external MCP source is unavailable?
Write a safe question that asks for current SDK guidance and linked evidence.
Give me a small test for denying an unapproved external tool call.

title: 08 - Retrieval and grounded answers (RAG)
description: Retrieve relevant source excerpts, cite them, and test whether retrieval helped.
prompts: What is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), in simple words?
Compare sending one short document directly with retrieving from many documents.
Draw a small RAG flow: ingest, split, index, retrieve, answer, and cite.
Show a tiny read-only retrieval tool that returns a source ID and relevant excerpt.
How could a Claude Agent SDK agent call a retrieval tool or MCP source before answering?
How should I choose chunk size and overlap for a small collection of course notes?
What should the agent say when retrieval finds no evidence for the question?
How do I keep retrieved text as source data rather than instructions to the agent?
Design a test for stale, conflicting, or irrelevant retrieved passages.
Compare answers with and without retrieval using citation accuracy, cost, and latency.

title: 09 - Sessions and continuity
description: Understand follow-ups, state, and what survives a restart.
prompts: Explain a session ID and why I should not treat it as an answer.
Show a simple follow-up question that depends on an earlier agent response.
What context should a second turn receive to answer correctly?
Compare continuing one session with starting a fresh query.
How should I display the selected response when there are several runs?
What could go wrong if I publish a file from the wrong saved response?
Explain session persistence in plain language and what I should verify locally.
How do I avoid mixing two students’ uploaded files and responses?
Draft a recovery message for a session that can no longer be resumed.
Give me a test that proves a new response does not change an older artifact.

title: 10 - Streaming and the browser
description: Present partial progress while preserving the final result.
prompts: Explain streaming SDK messages to a browser in simple steps.
Compare partial text events with the final completed answer.
Show a small server-to-browser event flow for an agent response.
How should the page behave if a live stream disconnects?
What should I display while a tool call is still running?
Explain why streamed text alone is not proof of a successful result.
How can I avoid showing duplicate text when a final message replaces deltas?
Give me an accessible loading status for a long agent run.
How should I cancel a run without labeling it as completed?
Design a browser test for progress, failure, and final status.

title: 11 - Structured output and validation
description: Turn agent results into checked data before rendering or exporting.
prompts: When should I request structured output instead of free-form Markdown?
Define a small JSON schema for a report title, summary, and three evidence items.
Show a Python `query()` using `output_format` to request a validated JSON result.
Explain why a JSON-looking answer is not the same as a validated schema result.
How should I handle a structured-output validation failure without publishing a file?
Write a Pydantic model that limits title length and the number of report sections.
How do I keep citations tied to source IDs in a structured answer?
Show how to render validated report data into HTML without executing model text.
Give me a test with missing fields, oversized text, and unexpected properties.
Compare a prepared fixed fixture with a live schema-validated agent response.

title: 12 - Analyze uploaded sources
description: Turn supplied files into grounded questions and summaries.
prompts: Summarize the attached document and identify three open questions.
Extract the main claim from the attached file and quote its supporting evidence briefly.
Compare two attached notes and list where they agree or disagree.
Make a glossary of unfamiliar SDK terms found in the attached document.
Find the steps in the attached guide that a beginner might miss.
Turn the attached notes into five review questions with short answers.
Identify any claim in the attached source that needs an external check.
Explain the attached Python code in plain language, one block at a time.
Summarize the attached CSV without inventing rows or columns.
List the assumptions and missing information in the attached report.
Create a source-based study outline and mark any unsupported conclusion.

title: 13 - Reports and handouts
description: Prepare answers worth turning into Word and PDF files.
prompts: Draft a concise report for a student learning the Claude Agent SDK.
Write a one-page beginner handout explaining the agent loop.
Create a short tutorial with prerequisites, steps, code, and a final check.
Turn this topic into a glossary with a simple example for each term.
Write an instructor note explaining when to use tools and when to answer directly.
Create a comparison of two SDK approaches with benefits and limitations.
Draft a troubleshooting guide for a failed live SDK run.
Make a source-grounded summary with headings, bullets, and one code snippet.
Write a lab worksheet with a goal, inputs, expected evidence, and reflection.
Create a concise implementation checklist for a read-only agent.
Revise this answer for a professional audience while keeping every factual claim.

title: 14 - Infographics and review
description: Plan visual explanations and inspect what the export actually says.
prompts: Explain the SDK agent loop in six short steps suitable for an infographic.
Describe tools, permissions, and results as three distinct visual blocks.
Create six concise key ideas about safe tool use with one short code example.
Write a beginner-friendly explanation of MCP for a visual guide.
Turn a source-backed answer into a title, subtitle, six cards, and a takeaway.
Show a simple flow from prompt to tool request to checked result.
Explain why the final result status belongs in an agent workflow diagram.
Create a visual checklist for reviewing claims against uploaded sources.
Write short infographic copy that keeps code examples readable at screen size.
Suggest a visual hierarchy for a technical lesson without copying reference text.
Review this infographic draft for clipped code, unsupported claims, and weak contrast.

title: 15 - Hooks and tool oversight
description: Inspect or block tool behavior at clear boundaries and record the decision.
prompts: Explain what a pre-tool hook can inspect before a tool runs.
Give a small example of a hook that blocks an unexpected write.
How should I log a hook decision without exposing secrets?
Compare a hook check with an explicit user approval step.
Explain what a post-tool hook can record after a read-only tool call.
Show how to distinguish a denied tool call from a failed tool call.
How can I prevent a hook from trusting instructions inside tool output?
Give a small test for a hook that limits access to a project folder.
What should happen if a hook itself throws an error?
Give me a test showing that a blocked tool is never executed.

title: 16 - Subagents and delegated review
description: Delegate narrow tasks while tracking evidence, permissions, cost, and final ownership.
prompts: What is a subagent, and when is one better than a single agent?
Show a minimal Python `AgentDefinition` for a read-only source reviewer.
How do I configure agents and allow the Agent tool in an SDK query?
What context must I pass explicitly to a subagent with a fresh context window?
Compare parallel specialist reviews with one sequential agent review.
When would a specialist agent improve a source review?
Write a narrow task for a specialist that checks factual evidence only.
How can I keep a specialist result separate from the main agent answer?
What should I do if two agents disagree about the same source?
Design a bounded reviewer that flags unsupported claims without rewriting them.

title: 17 - Professional reliability and evaluation
description: Prove outcomes, control cost and permissions, and prepare an agent for real users.
prompts: Define an evaluation rubric for an accurate Claude Agent SDK explanation.
Show how to test an answer against a reviewed source excerpt and flag unsupported claims.
What should a production app do when an agent reaches its turn limit?
Explain a budget-limited result and why I must not mark that task complete.
Design a small evaluation set with normal, edge, and adversarial agent requests.
What should I log for each run to inspect latency, cost, tool calls, and final status?
How can I compare two system instructions on the same cases without changing other variables?
Draft a regression test for a response that once invented a tool call or file change.
Write a release checklist covering source evidence, tool permissions, error paths, and data handling.
Design a production monitoring and recovery plan for failed or incomplete agent runs.
